candidates.title: Addressing mental health need after COVID-19: a systematic review of remote EMDR therapy studies as an emerging option.
candidates.finding: Sixteen articles with 1,231 participants cover remote individual, group and computerised interventions.
candidates.limitation: Heterogeneous designs include uncontrolled studies; this is not a randomised comparison of delivery methods.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: The immediate and follow-up effects of EMDR therapy for adults with post-traumatic stress disorder: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
candidates.proposedSection: EMDR for PTSD and related mental-health outcomes
candidates.finding: Sixty-five studies with 3,342 participants include immediate and follow-up PTSD outcomes.
candidates.limitation: Comparator and trauma type influence results; overlapping trials in earlier reviews are not new independent evidence.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: Clinical and Cost-Effectiveness of Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
candidates.proposedSection: EMDR for PTSD and related mental-health outcomes
candidates.finding: Eight clinical RCTs include 794 children and adolescents; one additional study examines cost-effectiveness.
candidates.limitation: Most comparisons use waitlist or usual care; limited active-comparator and economic evidence. EMDR UK funding is disclosed.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: Remote EMDR versus CBT for PTSD after the Kahramanmaraş earthquakes: a randomized trial.
candidates.finding: Eighty-nine earthquake survivors were allocated to remote EMDR, CBT or waitlist.
candidates.limitation: Benefits against waitlist do not establish EMDR superiority or equivalence to CBT; verify follow-up and masking in the full methods.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: The effectiveness of online Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing 2.0 Group Protocol on post-traumatic stress disorders symptoms, depression, anxiety, and stress in individuals who have experienced a traffic accident: a randomized-controlled study.
candidates.finding: Online EMDR 2.0 group delivery after traffic accidents produced advantages on several anxiety, stress and trauma measures.
candidates.limitation: A small non-clinical sample and one-month follow-up; between-group differences were not significant for depression or intrusion.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: The use of the "group traumatic episode protocol (G-TEP) " in an outpatient randomized and hospital setting: Implementation and effects in heterogeneous patient samples.
candidates.journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
candidates.design: Randomised delayed-waitlist trial and separate hospital implementation study
candidates.finding: A 44-person outpatient study and a 23-person hospital study extend evidence on group implementation.
candidates.limitation: The hospital component is distinct from the randomised outpatient component. Verify exact session structure and masking before grading.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: Trauma-focused treatments for refugee children and adolescents with PTSD: a three-arm randomized controlled trial comparing the efficacy of EMDR and KIDNET versus a waitlist control group (the KIEM study).
candidates.journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health
candidates.proposedSection: EMDR for PTSD in refugees and asylum seekers
candidates.finding: Ninety-six refugee children aged 8–18 were allocated to EMDR, KIDNET or waitlist; both active treatments improved PTSD outcomes.
candidates.limitation: Small arms and different dropout rates limit comparative claims. Outcomes do not establish treatment equivalence.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: The effect of eye movement desensitization on neurocognitive functioning compared to retrieval-only in PTSD patients: a randomized controlled trial.
candidates.finding: Ninety-one patients received eye movement desensitisation or retrieval alone; no additional neurocognitive benefit from eye movements was found.
candidates.limitation: The tested neurocognitive endpoints and component intervention do not represent every outcome or the full clinical protocol.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: Efficacy of eye movement desensitization and reprocessing for anxiety: An umbrella review and meta-meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
candidates.proposedSection: EMDR for PTSD and related mental-health outcomes
candidates.finding: Eleven meta-analyses report an average anxiety reduction, with a smaller advantage against active psychological treatments.
candidates.limitation: Most comparisons involve PTSD, nine reviews were rated low or critically low quality, and heterogeneity was substantial.
candidates.status: Candidate for integration; abstract/metadata screened; full methods and masking appraisal pending

candidates.title: The effectiveness of trauma-based therapies for Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal children and adolescents in out-of-home care
candidates.journal: First Nations Health and Wellbeing – The Lowitja Journal
candidates.proposedSection: Trauma-focused therapies for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and young people
candidates.finding: Analysis of 144 children and adolescents in the LINKS programme reports reduced difficulties and trauma symptoms, with positive findings for EMDR and parent–child interaction therapy.
candidates.limitation: No randomised treatment assignment or untreated control; the programme includes multiple therapies and cultural adaptations.
candidates.status: Open full text reviewed; candidate for integration
